title: When adding a field to an interface in content-schema.ts, add it to the Zod schema in validation.ts in the same commit, with `.strict()`
body: Zod mirrors the interfaces 1:1: one lowercase const per interface (`role` <-> `Role`, `media` <-> `Media`), same fields, same order, every object `.strict()`. Because of `.strict()`, a key present in content/data/content.es.json (or content.en.json) but missing from the Zod object THROWS in `pnpm run validate` and `pnpm test` instead of being dropped silently — that is the point, but it means an interface-only change breaks the first dataset edit that uses the field, possibly much later and in someone else's commit. Do both edits together. Never relax to `.passthrough()`/`.strip()` to make it pass. A new prose field is also picked up by the i18n tracker automatically (scripts/i18n-fields.ts uses a denylist), so expect `pnpm run test:i18n` to ask for its English translation; a new non-prose key must be added to `NOT_TEXT` there. The editor renders new fields from the schema via editor/schema-adapter.ts, which throws on Zod shapes it does not know.
not_derivable: Nothing links the TypeScript interface to its Zod twin at compile time; the mismatch only surfaces when data carrying the field arrives, and the 'same commit' rule was only written in CLAUDE.md.

evidence.summary: Line 19 comment: every object carries `.strict()`; an undeclared key throws.
NOT_TEXT denylist: any string key not listed is treated as translatable.
